newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
LALOO ISSUE, DALIT DEATHS ROCK HOUSE

Pandemonium reigned in parliament when the Congress party demanded the Maharashtra state government be dismissed and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) demanded the dismissal of Bihar state chief minister. The upper house of parliament was adjourned 15 minutes after the session began. In the lower house the BJP gave notice for an adjournment motion to discuss the situation in Bihar state. The Congress party gave a similar notice to discuss the police firing on untouchables in Bombay in Maharashtra state. The speaker admitted both the motions.
The Hindustan Times
SPEAKER SANGMA THREATENS TO QUIT

On the first day of the monsoon session of parliament P.A. Sangma, speaker of the lower house, threatened to quit to protest the unruly behaviour by members in the house. Sangma reprimanded members for unparliamentary behaviour. He said he felt ashamed of being the speaker of such a house and threatened to resign.
The Economic Times
SCHEME TO EXPEDITE DUTY REIMBURSEMENTS

The Revenue Department is working on an export-boosting scheme which may introduce insurance against revenue losses. The exporters now get their export-related revenue benefits only after the cargo is removed from ports. This may take one or two months after customs clearance at the inland container depots. To avoid this delay in getting export-related revenue benefits, the customs department is evolving a scheme whereby the benefits will be given to the exporters as soon as their goods are cleared at the inland container depots. As per the planned scheme the cargo will be ensured either by the exporter or the custodian for the value of the cargo as well as for the amount of duty or revenue reimbursed.
ISRAELI TEXTILE MILLS MAY MOVE SOME OPERATIONS TO INDIA

Some Israeli textile mills are planning to shift some of their operations to India to save labour costs estimated at 10:1 by the counsellor of economic affairs at the embassy of Israel in New Delhi. The plan is to split the manufacturing process so that the final product will remain Israeli under the rules of origin so as to qualify for duty free access under Israel's free trade agreements with the European Union and the United States. The counsellor said two demonstration farms for upgrading cotton had already been set up in India.
RELIANCE TO SEEK NOD TO RISE OVERSEAS STAKE TO 30 PCT

The Reliance Industries will seek its shareholders' permission to increase the limit on foreign institutional investor's (FIIs) holdings from 24 percent to 30 percent. This follows the stake of overseas investors in the Reliance touching 21 percent of the company's paid up equity capital of 4.58 billion rupees as on March 1997. This 21 percent includes an 8.5 percent equity held in the form of global depositary receipts which is not considered while calculating the ceiling for foreign institutional investor holdings. Based on an average price of 275 rupees during last year, the FII portfolio investment in Reliance will amount to 11 billion rupees.
Financial Express
GOVERNMENT PLANS RISK COMFORT FOR HIGHWAY PROMOTERS

The government plans to compensate private investors the entire unrecovered cost along with a suitable opportunity cost in highway projects in case the ownership is transferred or terminated ahead of the contracted schedule. The opportunity cost will be at a discount to the sum of assured annual return on investment over the period for which the project is contracted for with the private investors. The discount rate will be 12 percent. The opportunity cost provision will be inserted in the model contract that will soon be drawn up by the government.
Business Standard
BOURSE INDEX UP BY 64 POINTS

The Bombay bourse's sensitive index closed 64.84 points higher at 4251.13. The 50-share index National Bourse closed 27.45 points higher at 1200.70. Marketmen said the rise in share prices was fuelled by strong foreign institutional buying.
LENDING CORPORATION INTRODUCES SHORT TERM RATE

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) introduced a short term prime rate pegged at 12.5 percent to capitalise on the easy liquidity scenario. This short term rate will be a benchmark for pricing floating rate loans. The short term prime rate will enable long term borrowers to raise money at rates cheaper than the long term prime rate of 14 percent.
The Observer
MOODY GIVES BAA3 RATING TO INDIA

The rating of BAA3 was placed at the Indian sovereign ceiling for long term foreign currency denominated debt by international rating agency Moody. The slowdown in industrial growth and export growth coupled with an unstable political environment have lead to an unfavourable outlook for India's credit rating, Moody said. India still has a high dependence on imported oil which may lead to deterioration in the current and trade accounts, Moody said while assessing the Power Finance Corporation's proposed $100 million Eurobonds.
